posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Jio and Airtel literally dominate the Indian mobile market

TRAI's August 2026 data shows that just these two companies control more than 77% of India's mobile subscriptions

Aircel, Telenor, Tata Docomo, Videocon, MTS, Reliance Communications and Loop have all disappeared as independent mobile operators

Vodafone and Idea had to merge just to survive

What's left is a market where two companies have enormous influence over pricing, coverage and service for hundreds of millions of Indians

And now, when Starlink wants to bring another internet coverage to India where people don't really have, some stupid people sitting comfortably in cities with high-speed internet are saying, “We don't want Starlink”

Who are you to make that decision for everyone else?

Just because you have reliable internet doesn't mean millions of Indians living in rural and remote areas have the same luxury

How can you sit in a city with fast internet and decide that people in remote villages shouldn't even have that choice?

If you don't want Starlink, don't buy it. Nobody is forcing you

But don't be stupid enough to think your personal preference should decide what the rest of India gets to use

As Elon said to Ambani:

"Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India"

Real competition puts pressure on pricing, improves consumer choice and creates opportunities to connect places that existing networks still struggle to reach

India deserves more choices
Let Indians decide 🇮🇳

posts.text:
Nearly one in three Indian schools lacked internet access in the 2025–26 academic year.

The Education Ministry’s UDISE+ report recorded internet facilities in 67.4% of schools. It lists 14,66,682 schools nationwide, with internet available in 9,89,191. That leaves 4,77,491 schools without it.

Starlink could help connect remote schools and give teachers and students access to more learning resources. A child’s opportunities should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom. 

Starlink has already connected more than 6 million students worldwide. This is another powerful reason to support Starlink in India.
